key_insight: Under uncertainty, a Local Electricity Market (LEM) coordinates PV and batteries more effectively than flat tariffs or real-time pricing, lowering customer and system costs while revealing that storage value depends strongly on placement and penetration levels.
engineering_relevance: For distribution-grid planning, the results suggest LEMs can reduce congestion and upgrade pressure, but only if battery deployment is sited and scaled alongside PV growth rather than added blindly.
method: Modeled PV uncertainty with an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process to preserve temporal correlation.
Used rolling-horizon alternating optimal power flow on the IEEE 123-node feeder.
Compared flat tariff, real-time pricing, and LEM across storage and solar penetration scenarios.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on the IEEE 123-node feeder shows LEM has the lowest customer and system costs under uncertainty and outperforms other market designs across most storage and solar penetration levels.
watch_item: At very low PV penetration, LEM can worsen customer outcomes, so market rollout should be coordinated with PV expansion and careful battery siting.
paper_title: Understanding the role and value of battery storage in renewables-rich distribution grids under uncertainty and different market paradigms
